title: Binary Number with Alternating Bits
statement: Return true if every pair of adjacent bits in the binary representation of a positive integer differs.
explanation: Compare each bit with the previously processed bit while shifting the number right.

title: Max Area of Island
statement: Given a binary grid, return the largest area of a connected island of 1s using four-directional adjacency.
explanation: Visit each land cell once, explore its connected component, and track the largest component size.

title: Count Binary Substrings
statement: Count non-empty substrings with equal numbers of consecutive 0s and 1s where all 0s and all 1s are grouped together.
explanation: Track consecutive group lengths; each adjacent pair of groups contributes the minimum of their lengths.

title: Degree of an Array
statement: Return the minimum length of a contiguous subarray having the same degree as the whole array.
explanation: Track each value’s frequency and first/last positions, then minimize the span among values attaining maximum frequency.

title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
statement: Return the subtree rooted at the node whose value equals val, or null if no such node exists.
explanation: Compare val with the current node and continue into only the relevant BST subtree.

title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
approach: Insert at the first null child
statement: Insert val into a BST and return the root, preserving the BST property.
explanation: Follow comparisons until the appropriate child pointer is null, then attach a new node there.

title: Binary Search
statement: Return the index of target in a sorted array, or -1 if absent.
explanation: Maintain an inclusive low/high interval and discard the half that cannot contain the target.

title: To Lower Case
statement: Convert an ASCII string to lowercase.
explanation: Use the language’s lowercase conversion for the given ASCII letters.

title: 1-bit and 2-bit Characters
approach: Parse bits from left to right
statement: Given a bit array where 0 encodes one-bit character and 10 or 11 encodes two-bit character, return whether the last character is a one-bit character.
explanation: Advance one position for a leading 0 and two positions for a leading 1; check whether parsing ends at the final bit.

title: Find Pivot Index
statement: Return an index where the sum of elements to its left equals the sum of elements to its right, or -1 if none exists.
explanation: Maintain total sum and a running left sum; at each index compare left sum with total minus left sum and current value.
